mainTopic: The בכור's double portion: improvements made after a protest, pressed fruit, and giving up the extra share
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier list: if the בכור himself owed his father money, the extra share of that loan is split. Then רב הונא quotes רב אסי: a בכור who protested against his brothers improving the estate gets his double share of the improved value. רבה limits this to picking grapes or olives, while רב יוסף says it applies even after they were pressed into wine or oil. The גמרא asks how this can be, since grapes that became wine are a new item. It answers, using רב עוקבא בר חמא's explanation of a ruling of שמואל, that the brothers only pay the בכור for the loss to his grapes if the wine spoiled. Next, רב אסי rules that a בכור who took an equal share has given up his extra portion. רב פפא says he gave it up only in that field, because a בכור owns nothing extra before the division. רב פפי says he gave it up in the whole estate, because he does own it beforehand. The גמרא explains that both views were drawn from one ruling of רבא: a בכור who sold the undivided estate, including his late brother's share, has done nothing.

steps.title: A loan the firstborn owed his father is split
steps.stepSummary: The last item of an earlier list: when the בכור himself owed money to his father, the extra portion of that loan is divided between him and his brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a loan that the firstborn himself owes to the estate: they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of rulings from the previous discussion. If the בכור owed his father money, the brothers split the extra portion of that debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור gets פי שנים only in property the father actually held, not in property that was only due to come to him later. A debt the בכור owes is unclear: it is owed to the father, but the money is already in the בכור's own hands. Because the case is doubtful, they compromise and split the extra portion.

keyTerms.meaning: That is with him, meaning the בכור himself is the borrower
They split it, they divide it
Firstborn son, who inherits a double portion (פי שנים)

phrases.english: And a loan that is with him: they divide it.
phrases.notes: "With him" means the בכור himself borrowed the money from his father, so he is the one who owes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a list of rulings that began before this section, on which kinds of property give the בכור a double share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan the בכור owed his father is a doubtful case, so the brothers split the extra portion.

steps.title: A firstborn's protest against improvements counts
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב אסי: if the בכור protested against his brothers improving the estate, his protest works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב אסי: A firstborn who protested has protested, and his protest is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב אסי rules that if the בכור objects to his brothers improving the estate before it is divided, his objection counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בכור does not get a double share of the שבח, the added value the heirs themselves create after the father's death. רב אסי adds that if the בכור protested and the brothers improved it anyway, they cannot cut him out of the gain. He takes his double share of the improved value.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole debate that follows between רבה and רב יוסף about how far the protest reaches.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav Asi said:
A firstborn who protested has protested.
phrases.notes: In other words, his protest works. He objected to the brothers improving the estate before it was divided.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: בְּכוֹר שֶׁמִּיחָה – מִיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the בכור and improvements made by the heirs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the בכור protested against the estate being improved, he receives a double share of the improved value.

steps.title: רבה limits רב אסי to simple harvesting
steps.stepSummary: רבה says רב אסי's rule makes sense when the brothers only picked grapes or olives, but not when they pressed them into wine or oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רב אסי's reasoning makes sense with grapes that they harvested, or olives that they picked. But if they pressed them, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה narrows רב אסי's rule. Picking the fruit is covered by the protest, but pressing it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When grapes or olives are only picked, they are still the same fruit, so the בכור can claim his share of them. Pressing turns them into something new, wine or oil. רבה holds that this change takes the improvement out of the protest, so the בכור gets no double share of it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is reasonable

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִסְתַּבֵּר טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי
phrases.english: Rabba said: Rav Asi's reasoning makes sense
with grapes, and they harvested them,
olives, and they picked them;
but if they pressed them, not.
phrases.notes: Pressing turns grapes into wine and olives into oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִסְתַּבֵּר טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far רב אסי's ruling reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The protest works only when the fruit stays the same (picked). Once it is pressed into wine or oil, the בכור gets no double share.

steps.title: רב יוסף: even pressed fruit is included
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees with רבה and applies רב אסי's rule even after the fruit was pressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: Even if they pressed them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the opposite view. Even if the brothers made wine or oil, the בכור who protested still gets his double share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יוסף, the protest covers every improvement, even one that changes the fruit into a new product. This is a direct argument with רבה about whether the change from fruit to wine or oil matters here.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: Even if they pressed them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור who protested gets a double share even after the grapes or olives were pressed.

steps.title: Challenge: grapes became wine, a total change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף: once the grapes have become wine, the item has completely changed, so how can the בכור claim it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if they pressed them?! At first it was grapes, and now it is wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's view. Turning grapes into wine is a total change, so the בכור should lose his claim to the improvement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a שינוי, a real change in an object, gives ownership to the person who made the change. A גזלן, for example, owns the stolen item after changing it and only pays its value. Grapes becoming wine is exactly such a change, so the brothers should own the gain, and the בכור's protest should not help.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is aimed only at רב יוסף. It actually supports רבה's view that pressing ends the claim.

phrases.english: Even if they pressed them?!
At first it was grapes, and now it is wine!
phrases.notes: A change this big normally means whoever made the change now owns it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's statement in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that the protest applies even after pressing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Turning grapes into wine is a complete שינוי, which normally gives the one who made it ownership, the same way a גזלן acquires a stolen item. So the brothers should own the improvement, and the בכור should have no double share in it.

steps.title: רב יוסף meant payment for damaged grapes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's rule follows רב עוקבא בר חמא: the brothers pay the בכור for the damage to his grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף meant what רב עוקבא בר חמא said: they must give the בכור payment for the damage to his grapes. Here too, they pay him for the damage to his grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5. רב יוסף did not mean the בכור takes a double share of the wine itself. He meant the brothers must pay him for the loss to his share of the grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that wine is a totally new item, so the בכור cannot claim it. The answer moves the בכור's claim away from the wine and back to the original grapes. The case is one where the wine spoiled and became worth less than the grapes were, so the brothers owe him the value they ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same applies in this case

phrases.english: As Rav Ukva bar Chama said:
to give him payment for the damage to his grapes;
phrases.notes: This is talking about a case where the wine went bad and became worth less than the grapes.

phrases.english: here too, they give him
payment for the damage to his grapes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 against רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case and the claim: the claim is payment for damage, not a share of the wine.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף seemed to give the בכור a double share of the wine, which is a new item.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף means the brothers pay the בכור for the loss to his grapes when the wine spoiled.

steps.title: Where was רב עוקבא בר חמא's rule said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the original setting of רב עוקבא בר חמא's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where was רב עוקבא בר חמא's statement said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב עוקבא בר חמא first said his rule. This sets up the next step, which shows the original source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was just borrowed to explain רב יוסף. Now the גמרא goes back to show its original context, so we can see that it fits the same kind of case.

phrases.english: Where was it said,
the statement of Rav Ukva bar Chama?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule that was used in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original context of רב עוקבא בר חמא's statement.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling on picked and pressed fruit
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the בכור takes a double portion of inherited grapes or olives that were picked, even if they were pressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said on this ruling of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: a בכור and a regular son whose father left them grapes, and they picked them, or olives, and they harvested them. The בכור takes a double portion, even if they pressed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting שמואל's ruling, which is where רב עוקבא בר חמא's statement belongs. שמואל says the בכור still takes a double portion even after the fruit was pressed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking the fruit does not cancel the בכור's double portion. שמואל goes further and says this is true even after pressing. That is the same surprising idea as רב יוסף's view, and it will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son, who gets a double portion

phrases.aramaic: אַהָא – דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: On this, which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
A firstborn and an ordinary son
whose father left them grapes, and they picked them;
or olives, and they harvested them,
the firstborn takes a double portion,
even if they pressed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by quoting the original ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The statement was said about שמואל's ruling on grapes and olives that were picked and even pressed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור takes a double portion of inherited fruit that was picked, even if it was pressed.

steps.title: Grapes have become wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the grapes have turned into wine, a different item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if they pressed them?! At first they were grapes, and now it is wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling the same way it challenged רב יוסף. Once grapes become wine, how can the בכור claim a double share of it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers improved and changed the item, and the wine is a new thing. A בכור does not get a double share of value that was added after the father died, so the ruling looks hard to understand.

phrases.english: They pressed them?!
At first they were grapes, and now it is wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last clause of שמואל's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's words 'even if they pressed them'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pressing turns grapes into wine, a new item, so the בכור should have no double share in it.

steps.title: Payment for the damage to his grapes
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא בר חמא explains שמואל: the other brother pays the בכור for the damage to his grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא בר חמא said: it means they must give him payment for the damage to his grapes.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא בר חמא answers that שמואל did not give the בכור a double share of the wine. He meant the brother pays the בכור for the loss to his share of the grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the original place of the answer that step 6 borrowed. The case is where the wine spoiled and was worth less than the grapes, so the בכור is paid back the value of his extra share of the grapes.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב יוסף and שמואל mean the same thing: the בכור is not given a share of the wine. If the wine spoiled, he is paid back for his share of the grapes.

phrases.english: Mar Ukva bar Chama said:
It means to give him payment for the damage to his grapes.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the ruling as a claim for damage, not a share of the new item.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to give the בכור a double share of the wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בכור is paid for the damage to his grapes when the wine went bad.

steps.title: A בכור who took an ordinary share gave up
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that a בכור who took a share like a regular brother has given up his extra portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: a בכור who took a share like a regular son has given up his extra portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a rule from רב אסי. If a בכור divided with his brothers and took only an equal share, he has given up his double portion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By accepting an equal share, the בכור shows he is letting go of his right. The rule does not yet say how far this giving-up reaches, and the next step asks about exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: A share like an ordinary son

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
A firstborn who took a share like an ordinary son
has given up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי בְּכוֹר שֶׁנָּטַל חֵלֶק כְּפָשׁוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a בכור giving up his extra portion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור who takes an equal share has given up his extra portion.

steps.title: What does 'given up' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far the בכור's giving-up reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he has given up' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב אסי meant by 'given up'. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about scope. Did the בכור give up only in the property he already divided, or in the whole estate?

phrases.english: What does "has given up" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of one word in רב אסי's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far the בכור's giving-up reaches.

steps.title: He gave up only in that field
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, quoting רבא, says the בכור gave up only in the field that was divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: he gave up only in that field.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first answer. The בכור gave up his extra portion only in the field he already divided equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, the giving-up is narrow. The בכור still keeps his double portion in the rest of the estate.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
He gave up in that field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The giving-up applies only to the field that was divided.

steps.title: He gave up in all the property
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, quoting רבא, says the בכור gave up his extra portion in the whole estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: he gave up in all of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי gives a second, wider answer. By taking an equal share, the בכור gave up his extra portion in the entire estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers quote רבא, but they report him differently. רב פפי makes the giving-up cover everything, not just the one field.

keyTerms.meaning: All of the property, every part of it

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא and רב פפי are two different אמוראים with very similar names. Both quote רבא here, but they disagree.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
He gave up in all of the property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 12 than step 13 does.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The giving-up applies to the whole estate.

steps.title: Why רב פפא limits it to that field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב פפא holds the בכור has no extra portion before the division, so he waived only what reached his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא that he gave up in that field because he holds that a בכור has nothing before the division. What came into his hands, he waived. The rest, he did not waive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב פפא's view in order to explain his reason. A בכור's extra portion only becomes his at the division, so he can waive only the part that has already been divided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the בכור does not yet own his extra share in property that has not been divided, he cannot give it up. In the field that was divided, he took his share and let the extra go, so only that field is waived.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the argument about scope to a basic question: does the בכור own his extra share before the estate is divided?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
he gave up in that field,

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָבַר: אֵין לוֹ לַבְּכוֹר קוֹדֶם חֲלוּקָּה;
phrases.english: because he holds: the firstborn has nothing before the division;
and what came into his hands, he waived;
the rest, he did not waive.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר אֵין לוֹ לַבְּכוֹר קוֹדֶם חֲלוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats רב פפא's view from step 13 to explain the reason behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור has no extra portion before the division, so he waives only what he already received.

steps.title: Why רב פפי says the waiver covers the whole estate
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, quoting רבא, says the בכור gave up his extra share in all the property. The reason is that a בכור owns his extra share even before the division.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: the בכור gave up his extra portion in all the property. He holds that a בכור has his extra portion even before the division. So once he gave it up in this field, he gave it up in all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב פפי's view, and this time it adds his reason, just as step 15 gave the reason for רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב פפי, the בכור's extra share is already his before anything is divided. So when he took an equal share in one field, he was giving up something he really owned, and that waiver reaches the whole estate. רב פפא disagrees because for him the extra share does not exist yet before the division.

keyTerms.meaning: before the division of the estate

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole מחלוקת depends on one question: does a בכור own his extra share before the division, or not?

phrases.english: And Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
He relinquished in all of the property entirely,
phrases.notes: He means the בכור gave up his extra share in the whole estate, not only in the field they divided.

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָבַר: יֵשׁ לוֹ לִבְכוֹר קוֹדֶם חֲלוּקָּה;
phrases.english: for he holds: a firstborn has his portion before the division;
and since he waived in this one,
he waived in all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר: יֵשׁ לוֹ לִבְכוֹר קוֹדֶם חֲלוּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 15. That step gave רב פפא's reason, and this one gives רב פפי's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור owns his extra portion before the division, so waiving it in one field waives it in the entire estate.

steps.title: This מחלוקת was learned by inference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבא never stated the views of רב פפא and רב פפי directly. Both were drawn from one of his rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagreement between רב פפי and רב פפא was not said openly. It was figured out by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to tell the story of the case that both אמוראים learned from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far it sounded as if רבא gave two different statements. Now we learn that he gave one ruling in a real case, and each אמורא read a different reason into it. This line opens the story.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference, drawn out from something else

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture רבא stating two opposite rulings. He gave one ruling, and the מחלוקת is about how to understand it.

phrases.english: And this dispute of Rav Pappi and Rav Pappa
was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 13 through 16 laid out the two views. Here the גמרא explains where those views come from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רב פפא and רב פפי comes from inference based on a ruling of רבא, not from statements he made outright.

steps.title: The story: the בכור sold the estate before dividing it
steps.stepSummary: A בכור sold both his own share and his late brother's share. The buyers then hit the orphans who came to eat dates, and the relatives protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a בכור who went and sold his own property and his brother's property. The orphans of the פשוט went to eat dates from those buyers, and the buyers hit them. The relatives said to the buyers: Is it not enough that you bought their property? You also hit them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the real case that רבא ruled on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The estate had not been divided yet, and the בכור sold all of it, including the share of his brother, the פשוט. The orphans felt the fields were still partly theirs, so they took dates. The buyers treated them like thieves. This sets up the question of whether the בכור's sale was valid.

phrases.english: For there was a certain firstborn who went
and sold the property, his own and that of the ordinary brother.
The orphans, sons of the ordinary brother, went
to eat dates from those buyers,
and they hit them.
The relatives said to them:
Is it not enough that you bought their property,
but you also hit them?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָהוּא בְּכוֹר דַּאֲזַל זַבֵּין נִכְסֵי דִּידֵיהּ וּדְפָשׁוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the case that step 17 said the מחלוקת was drawn from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case: a בכור sold the undivided estate, including his brother's share, and the buyers hit the orphans who came to take dates.

steps.title: רבא rules that the בכור's sale did nothing
steps.stepSummary: They came before רבא, and he ruled that the בכור's sale has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבא. He said to them: He has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his ruling in the case. This short ruling is the source that רב פפא and רב פפי each read in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the sale is worthless, but he does not say why, and he does not say whether it fails for the whole estate or only part of it. That open question is where the two readings come from.

keyTerms.meaning: he has done nothing; the act has no legal effect

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's whole ruling is just לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם. Both רב פפא and רב פפי build their views from this one ruling.

phrases.english: They came before Rava,
he said to them:
He has done nothing.
phrases.notes: He means the בכור's sale has no legal effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא, אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the ruling on the story told in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור's sale of the undivided estate has no legal effect.
